profile.primaryMotivation: Get a credible budget figure quickly, so the conversation with a mason starts from a known number, without spending time learning construction vocabulary or filling in long forms.

generated.primaryMotivation: Get a credible budget figure quickly, so the conversation with a mason starts from a known number, without spending time learning construction vocabulary or filling in long forms.
generated.decisionStyle: Scans quickly for the first clear signal and leans toward speed, accepting some risk. Seldom double-checks unless something looks off, generally trusts on-screen labels and indicators, and prefers to handle things alone, escalating only as a last resort. Decisions rest on the most prominent number or label available; a plausible-looking answer is accepted rather than investigated.
generated.attentionPattern: Attention goes to headings, numbers, totals and primary actions; explanatory paragraphs, footnotes and help text are skimmed or skipped. Technical terms are passed over unless they block progress. Figures are compared quickly against a rough mental expectation rather than reviewed line by line.
generated.trustPattern: Generally takes on-screen labels, computed quantities and prices at face value. Trust drops only when something visibly contradicts itself, such as a total that changes without explanation or a figure that seems wildly off, or when the product repeatedly asks for the same information.
generated.behaviorUnderPressure: Under time pressure, reads even less and accepts prefilled values as given. Long forms or extra steps trigger impatience; accepts an account requirement but expects it to be short, and fatigue rises quickly if sign-up asks for many fields. After repeated errors, gives up rather than troubleshooting.
generated.toleranceForAmbiguity: Fairly high tolerance for ambiguity about details (exact material specifications, unexplained jargon) as long as a figure and a clear next action are visible. Low tolerance for ambiguity about what to do next or whether a result has actually been produced: when the next action is not visible, stops.
commonWrongAssumptions: Assumes the computed budget is an all-inclusive price (labour and delivery included) when it may cover materials only.
Assumes prefilled values such as thickness or concrete dosage suit their own job without questioning them.
Assumes displayed material prices are current local Mayotte prices, whether or not a date or source is shown.
Assumes technical line items such as hérisson or treillis soudé are optional extras that can be dropped to lower the budget.
Assumes account creation will be a one-step formality and that the figure seen before sign-up is already the final quote.
Assumes both calculator modes produce equivalent results, so the shortest-looking one is as good as the other.
Assumes any supplier listed in the directory stocks the needed materials and delivers to the site.
generated.calibrationNotes: Pole 1a of a contrasted pair with btm-particulier-prudent. This profile sits at pace 1 and trust 1, the partner at pace 4 and trust 4; priority, verification and escalation are held at 1 here so outcome differences can be attributed to reading depth and trust. Expect this user to reach a figure fast, to miss caveats written in body text and to accept prefilled values; failures should surface as unnoticed misunderstandings rather than explicit hesitation. Technical proficiency is high, so interface-mechanics friction should be rare; friction should come from jargon, form length and unclear next steps. Will create an account when the product requires it, but reacts badly to long forms.

productContext.businessDomain: Construction quotes and local building-material supply, Mayotte (976)
productContext.manualDescription: BTM (btm.yt) is a French-language construction-quote web platform for Mayotte. Users pick a structure (wall, slab, foundation, terrace) and BTM computes quantities and budget, and points to local material suppliers (directory with call, directions and email). The quote calculator has two modes: 'Selon mes mesures' (give dimensions, BTM computes quantities, for laypeople) and 'Je sais ce qu'il me faut' (pick materials and quantities yourself, for knowledgeable users). Generating the quote requires an account. Also: supplier directory with search, category filters and a delivers-to-site filter; customer reviews; help chat widget. Mobile-first; French is often a second language for users.
productContext.knownPrimaryUsers: Private individuals building family homes or garages, independent masons and artisans
productContext.knownWorkflows: Choosing a structure type; quote calculator in two modes (Selon mes mesures, Je sais ce qu'il me faut); account creation required to generate the quote; supplier directory with search, category filters and delivers-to-site filter; reading customer reviews; help chat widget
productContext.knownRiskAreas: Sign-up wall mid-funnel; technical jargon (hérisson, treillis, semelles); trust in computed prices

descriptions.End user: Private individual planning a small family construction job who wants a budget figure before calling a mason. Scans quickly for the headline number, trusts on-screen labels, decides fast and compares figures rather than reading explanations. Hesitates only when terminology blocks progress or a form feels long, and prefers to work things out alone before asking for help.

expertise.interpretation: Low domain expertise: does not know construction terms such as hérisson, treillis soudé or semelles, nor typical concrete thicknesses or dosages, and cannot judge whether a computed quantity is plausible. High technical proficiency: at ease with web forms, mobile layouts and account creation, so interface mechanics rarely slow them down. Occasional user of online quote calculators and comparison tools, with no prior exposure to BTM.
